title: The same forever (Hebrews 13:1–8)
hookLine: keep loving; show hospitality; remember prisoners; Jesus Christ the same yesterday, today and forever
tomorrow: what do you write first to friends scattered far from home?

cards: The doorbell. A delivery driver in the rain, a new kid at the lunch table, the neighbor you've waved at for a year and never met. Who might be an angel at your door, and how would you know?
Hebrews answers, and the answer is: you wouldn't. "Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares." Unawares.
Nobody got a sign. They just opened the door.

teach.b: The whole list is like that: people easy to forget. It opens, "Let brotherly love continue." Then strangers.
Then prisoners: "Remember them that are in bonds, as bound with them; and them which suffer adversity, as being yourselves also in the body." Not pity from a distance.
As if the chains were on your own wrists, because you have a body too.
Then money: "be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee." Contentment rests on a promise, not a balance.
And then one sentence standing on its own: "Jesus Christ the same yesterday, and to day, and for ever."

teach.h: THE WEEK ENDS WHERE IT BEGAN.
teach.b: Look how this week ends where it began.
It opened with a priest who never hands off, and it closes on the same one, unchanged. Guests come and go. Prisoners wait.
Teachers pass on. Hebrews sets one who doesn't change in the middle of all of it, and hangs the whole list on him.

how: Christians visit and pray for prisoners through church prison ministries, welcome guests and newcomers, and some churches carve Hebrews 13:8 over a door or an altar.

o: a promise that your life will never change
the rule that church worship must never change
Jesus, unchanged while everything around him changes

Hebrews sets 'the same forever' inside a list about guests and prisoners
the unchanging one stands in the middle of changing people.

games.q: a new family moves in across the street, and their kid stands alone at the bus stop every morning. you don't know them at all. what fits Hebrews 13?
o: wait until you're sure they're safe and worth it.
say hello; some have entertained angels unawares.
leave it to the church; welcome is a pastor's job.
games.why: be not forgetful to entertain strangers: Hebrews asks for the welcome first, without a sign or a guarantee.

practice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone who is locked up tonight, someone you know or someone you'll never meet. Rest your wrists on your knees and keep that person company, as bound with them, until the bell.
